1.explanation:
• util.js defines the formatBytes (and related) functions that convert a raw byte count into a human-readable string. It currently drops the fraction when it’s zero. By adjusting its NumberFormat options to always include at least one fraction digit (minimumFractionDigits: 1), “18 KiB” will become “18.0 KiB”.
• details-renderer.js is the component that renders table cells of type “bytes” by calling util.formatBytes. It’s the consumer of the formatting utility for the Transfer Size column, so it’s closely tied to how that output appears in the report.
1.bug_scenario: In the “Large JavaScript libraries” details table the Transfer Size column values are formatted by our byte-formatting utility such that “round” KiB values drop the “.0” decimal. For example, date-fns (18 × 1024 B) renders as “18 KiB” while luxon (20.4 KiB) renders correctly with “20.4 KiB”. This causes the numbers in the column to misalign and makes visual comparison harder, especially for users with low vision.

2.explanation:
• util.js (lighthouse-core/report/html/renderer/util.js) defines the formatBytes (or similar) function that turns a raw byte count into a human-readable string (e.g. “18 KiB”). Currently it omits “.0” for whole KiB values. This is exactly where you’d enforce “always show one decimal digit.”

• details-renderer.js (lighthouse-core/report/html/renderer/details-renderer.js) is the component that lays out the table rows and invokes util.formatBytes on every “bytes” cell. It’s indirectly responsible for rendering the sizes in the report. Although it doesn’t contain the formatting logic itself, it’s where the formatted output appears in the UI. Adjusting util.js will flow through here to fix the bug.
2.bug_scenario: In the “Large JavaScript libraries” details table, libraries whose transfer‐size in KiB is an integer (for example 18 KiB) are rendered without any decimal place ("18 KiB"), while non-integer sizes (for example 20.4 KiB) show one decimal. This misalignment in the "Transfer Size" column makes it harder to scan the table and poses an accessibility issue for users with low vision.
